transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for having me. I really appreciate you taking the time. Um, I'm hoping I'm in the right place. I'm sure it's probably just normal stress—I manage a health clinic, so things get a little busy—but... well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I've been having a little trouble staying on track at work lately? 

Like, I can sit down to start an EPIC quality report, or I'll be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I have every intention of tracking all the details. I really do. But within just a few minutes, my mind just sort of... drifts. I'll catch myself rereading the same numbers over and over, or I'll suddenly realize I kind of missed the whole point of the discussion. 

It’s a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I know I should be on top of it. I'm sure it's not the worst thing in the world, and I try to cover for it, but I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for my team. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you handle here?
Have you also noticed any restlessness, difficulty staying seated, or acting on impulse without thinking things through?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I try to be very professional at work. I sit through all my meetings, and I'm definitely not running around or anything like that. I'm usually the one trying to keep everyone else calm, you know? 

I might fidget a little bit with my pen, but I think everyone does that when they're trying to focus, right? I definitely don't act on impulse... I always try to be very careful and considerate before I make any decisions for the clinic. I hope I didn't give the impression that I was being disruptive or anything like that.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual or noticed a lack of energy, even after getting enough rest?

No, I wouldn't say I'm unusually tired. I mean, I get a little fatigued by the end of the day, but I think that's just normal for my age and having a busy job, right? I try to make sure I get my eight hours of sleep, and I usually wake up feeling okay. 

I'm definitely not walking around exhausted all the time or anything like that. I really try to keep my energy up for the staff. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even things you used to really look forward to?

Oh, no, definitely not. I'm not depressed or anything like that. I actually really enjoy my job, and I love spending time with my family on the weekends. I still look forward to our Sunday dinners and my morning walks. 

I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself sometimes when I can't seem to just focus on a simple report, but it doesn't make me sad or hopeless. I try to keep a really positive attitude. I know how important it is to keep morale up at the clinic, so I always try to bring a smile to work. I hope that's helpful? I just want to reassure you that I'm generally a very happy person.
Have you been having trouble organizing your tasks or keeping your work space and materials in order, especially when you're trying to focus on something important?

Oh, um, organizing? Well, I like to think I'm fairly organized. I mean, you have to be to run a clinic, right? I have my systems in place, and I try to keep my desk looking professional. 

Sometimes, you know, when it gets really busy, maybe a few papers pile up, or I might have to spend an extra minute looking for a specific file... but I think everyone's desk gets a little cluttered during a busy week, don't you think? I always make sure the important things are taken care of, though. I'd never let anything slip that would affect the patients or the staff. I hope that makes sense? I really do try my best to keep everything running smoothly.
Have you been forgetting things often in your daily life, like appointments, tasks, or where you put important items, even if they’re things you used to remember easily?

Oh, um, forgetting things? No, I wouldn't say I'm unusually forgetful. I mean, in my role managing the clinic, you really can't afford to miss appointments or forget important tasks, right? I rely on my planner and my digital calendar, of course, just to be thorough. 

I guess maybe once in a blue moon I might forget where I set my reading glasses down at home, but... well, I think everyone does that when they have a lot on their plate, don't you think? I really pride myself on being dependable for my staff and the patients. I hope that's okay to say? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm letting things slip through the cracks or anything like that.
Do you find it difficult to stay focused on tasks outside of work, such as reading a book at home or following through with chores, or does this mainly happen during work-related activities?

Oh, outside of work? Well, I think I do pretty well at home, honestly. I mean, after a long day at the clinic, I think it's perfectly normal to just want to relax and maybe not be perfectly focused on, you know, scrubbing baseboards or reading a heavy book. 

I do try to keep up with the house, of course. I want my family to have a nice environment. Sometimes I might start a load of laundry and then get distracted by making dinner, so the laundry might sit for a bit... but I always get to it eventually! And with reading, I usually just prefer lighter things or magazines now, which are easier to flip through. I think that's just part of getting older and having a busy life, don't you? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm neglecting my home life, because I really do try to be a good wife and mother. I just think the work tasks are where I notice the frustration a bit more, if that makes sense?
Can you think of a time outside of work, maybe at home or during a personal activity, where you also had real difficulty staying focused or finishing something you started?

Oh, um... a specific time outside of work? Honestly, I really can't think of anything that I'd call a real difficulty. I mean, like I mentioned with the laundry, sometimes things might take me a little longer if I'm trying to juggle a few different chores on a weekend, but... well, I think everyone gets a little sidetracked when they're just trying to catch up at home, don't you? 

I always make sure to finish whatever I've started before the day is over. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm leaving the house in a mess or, you know, failing at my responsibilities to my family. I take a lot of pride in making sure they have everything they need. I hope it's okay that I don't have a big example for you? I just... I really do feel like I manage my personal life pretty well, all things considered.
Can you describe how long these focus issues have been happening, and were they present before your work responsibilities became so demanding?

Oh, um... well, as for how long, I'd say it really just started after my last promotion. That was about two years and four months ago. Before that, I didn't have any trouble at all! I've always prided myself on being very organized and on top of my work. 

But with the promotion came a much larger portfolio, and... well, I suppose the sheer volume of it just started overwhelming the little organizational systems I used to rely on. I mean, it's a lot of new responsibility, and I think anyone would find it a little challenging to adjust to that much extra work, don't you think? I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or anything. I was so honored they trusted me with the bigger role, and I really do give it my all every single day. Does that make sense?
Do you notice that your difficulty staying focused tends to happen more often during tasks that are repetitive, boring, or require a lot of sustained attention?

Oh, well... I suppose so, yes. I mean, I think everyone finds those sorts of tasks a little tedious, right? 

But, um, if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses or trying to get out of doing my job—I do find myself putting off certain things. Like... the really dense policy reviews, or those long blocks of data analysis. I tend to push those to late in the day. 

It's just... the thought of having to sit down and do that much detailed reading and heavy thinking all at once, it almost feels physically hard to start. I know I need to do it, and I always make sure it gets done, of course! I'd never just ignore it. But... is it normal to feel that kind of resistance to the boring, repetitive parts of the job? I really try my best to push through it, I promise.
Do you ever notice these focus issues in situations where you’re really interested in the task or it’s something you enjoy, or does it only happen with tasks you find boring or overwhelming?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. If it's something I'm really interested in, or, you know, a project I actually enjoy, I don't have any trouble focusing at all. Actually, I can get completely absorbed in it! 

Like, if I'm working on a new patient care initiative at the clinic that I'm really passionate about, or even just doing something I love on the weekend, I can stay locked in for hours without even looking at the clock. So it really is just those... well, those tedious or overwhelming things I mentioned before. 

I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm just being selective or... or lazy about what I choose to pay attention to! I really do try to give my absolute best to every part of my job, even the dry parts. But yes, if I like the task, the focus is just naturally there. That's a good sign, isn't it? It shows I am capable of focusing when it matters, right?

Have you ever had trouble staying focused on tasks or activities that aren't particularly interesting to you, even in settings outside of work—like when you're listening to someone talk, reading something you don't find exciting, or trying to follow through on something that takes a lot of sustained effort?

Oh, um... well, I suppose it does happen sometimes outside of just the heavy paperwork. I mean, I think everyone’s mind wanders a little bit during long conversations, don't you? 

But, um... well, if I'm being completely honest, there are times when... when a medical director or one of my coordinators is talking directly to me. I'll be looking right at them, and I'm nodding, and I really am trying to listen! I want them to feel heard, of course. But then... well, I'll realize I have to ask them to repeat the action item because the words just... they just didn't stay with me. 

I always apologize and make sure I get the information right, though! I'd hate for them to think I don't care about what they're saying, because I really, truly do. It's just sometimes my brain sort of... slips away for a second. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible manager. It's just a little blip, and I always correct it right away. That's pretty normal, isn't it? Just a little momentary distraction?

Do you ever find yourself losing focus during everyday conversations or activities that aren’t work-related, like watching a movie, listening to a lecture, or even just having a casual chat with a friend?

Oh, um... outside of work? Well... I guess I haven't really noticed it being a huge problem in my personal life. I mean, if I'm chatting with a friend, I'm usually pretty engaged! I value my friendships so much, I'd hate to be the kind of person who tunes out when someone is sharing their day with me. 

Maybe... maybe occasionally if a movie is really slow, I might start thinking about my grocery list, but that's just multitasking, right? Everyone does that. Or if a lecture is incredibly dry... but I don't really go to many lectures these days anyway. 

So, no, I don't think it's a major issue when I'm just relaxing or spending time with people I care about. I try very hard to be present for my friends and family. That's the most important thing, don't you think? Being there for the people you love? I really do try my best to be a good listener for them.
Have these focus issues caused you significant distress or affected your performance at work or in your personal life in any way?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say *significant* distress. I mean, I still get things done! I really do try so hard to keep everything running smoothly. But... I suppose... 

Well, if I'm being completely honest, there have been a few little hiccups at work lately. Nothing I can't handle, of course! But... my delays with the paperwork have started affecting some of the clinic reporting deadlines. And, um, I hate to admit it, but it’s occasionally made other teams have to wait on me. I feel just awful about it when it happens. I never want to be the bottleneck, you know? I really pride myself on being a supportive manager. 

And, um... outside of work, I do help run these volunteer health workshops, which I absolutely love. But recently, I... well, I had to step back from leading some of the planning pieces. It just felt like I couldn't reliably keep all the moving parts going, and I didn't want to let the volunteers down. It was better for the program if someone else took the reins on that part. 

So, I guess it has affected things a little bit. But I'm working on it! I'm trying new organizational systems and really pushing myself to do better. That's the right attitude to have, isn't it? As long as I'm trying to fix it, it's not too terrible... right?
Can you recall any situations where you found yourself losing focus on a task or conversation even though you were genuinely interested or trying your hardest to stay engaged?

Oh, um... goodness. When I'm genuinely interested? 

Well, no, I don't think so. I mean, if I really care about what I'm doing, or if I'm talking to someone about something I love, I'm usually right there! I'm completely engaged. Like with the volunteer workshops I mentioned earlier—when I'm actually at the event, helping people face-to-face, I don't lose focus at all. It's really just the behind-the-scenes planning and the paperwork that gets a little fuzzy for me. 

I would feel just terrible if I started drifting off when someone was talking about something we were both really passionate about. That would seem so dismissive, wouldn't it? I never want to make anyone feel like I don't value what they're sharing. 

So, no, I can't really think of a time like that. I feel like if my heart is in it, my brain usually follows along just fine. That makes sense, doesn't it? It's mostly just the dry, repetitive things that trip me up... which I think is how most people operate, right?

Can you recall any instances where you had trouble staying focused on a task or activity that wasn’t boring or repetitive—something that should have held your interest, like a meeting with colleagues or a meaningful conversation?

Oh, um... instances where it wasn't boring, but I still lost focus? 

Well, no, I... I don't think so. I really do try my absolute hardest to be present, especially for meetings with my colleagues or if we're having a meaningful conversation. I mean, as a manager, it's my job to listen and support my team, and I take that responsibility very seriously. I would hate for them to think I wasn't paying attention to them when they needed me. That would be awful.

I feel like if something is important or if I'm talking to someone, I'm fully there. I really do care about the people I work with, and I want to make sure they feel heard. It's really just the... the paperwork and the data entry that I struggle with, like I mentioned before. 

So, I don't think I have trouble focusing when it's something that *should* hold my interest. I mean, if it's meaningful, I'm engaged. That's a good sign, isn't it? It means I'm still doing okay where it really counts, right?

Have you ever noticed yourself losing focus during tasks or conversations that are both important and interesting to you, such as a team brainstorming session, a meaningful conversation with a loved one, or a topic you're passionate about?

Oh, gosh... I feel terrible, I know you're asking this again and I really want to give you a helpful answer! But... um, honestly, no. I haven't noticed that happening. 

When it comes to my family, or a really exciting brainstorming session with my staff, I'm completely tuned in. I would just die of embarrassment if my husband or one of my team members was pouring their heart out and I just spaced out. I mean, maybe if a phone rings loudly right next to me I might glance over, but that's just human nature, isn't it? I always make sure the people I care about know they have my undivided attention. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a good example of that for you. I'm trying to be as thorough as I can... I'm answering these questions alright, aren't I?

Have you ever noticed that your difficulty focusing tends to improve when you're in a good mood or feeling particularly motivated, or does it seem to happen regardless of how you're feeling emotionally?

Oh... hmm. That's a really interesting question. I... I honestly haven't really tracked that. 

I mean, I always try my best to bring a positive attitude to the office, you know? Setting a good example for the staff is just so important to me. But as for whether being in a good mood actually changes how well I can get through those... those tedious administrative tasks... I'm really not sure I've noticed a pattern. 

I feel like even on my very best days, when I'm feeling wonderful and highly motivated to just sit down and finally clear off my desk, I still sort of... hit that same wall with the data entry and the spreadsheets. It just always seems to be a struggle, regardless of how upbeat I'm feeling. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a more specific answer for you. Maybe I should be paying closer attention to my moods when I'm working? I'm doing my best to give you what you need, I promise... is that a helpful answer at all?
Have you ever noticed yourself losing focus during short conversations or tasks that only take a few minutes, even if they’re simple and not particularly boring or overwhelming?

Oh, um, short conversations? Like just a quick chat or a simple task? 

Well, no, I... I really don't think so. I mean, if something only takes a few minutes, I can definitely power through it. I'm very mindful of people's time, especially my team's, so if someone just needs a quick answer or we're having a brief check-in, I am completely focused on them. I would feel just awful if I couldn't even pay attention for a two-minute conversation! That would seem so rude, wouldn't it? 

And for simple tasks, you know, if it's quick, I just get it done. It's really only the long, drawn-out things that trip me up. I try so hard to be efficient and present for the little things. 

I hope that makes sense? I feel like I keep telling you "no" to these questions, and I really don't want to be difficult or unhelpful. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can... am I giving you the kind of information you need?
Can you recall any specific moment where you lost focus on a task or conversation that you genuinely cared about, even if only briefly, despite trying to stay engaged?

Oh, dear... I know you're really trying to help me figure this out, and I want so badly to give you a specific moment like you're asking for. But... I just can't think of one. 

If it's something I genuinely care about, I just don't let myself drift off. My staff at the clinic rely on me so much, and my family means the world to me. I would feel absolutely terrible if I checked out on them, even for just a second, you know? I pride myself on being a good listener for the people who need me. I suppose if I was completely and utterly exhausted, maybe my mind might wander for a split second? But no, I really can't picture a specific time where I truly wanted to be engaged and just... lost it. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself and not giving you the examples you're looking for today. I promise I'm really searching my memory. Am I making this too difficult for you?
